brief: BTIG's technical strategist argues equity market breadth is deteriorating beneath continued strength in AI/semiconductor names, and links this to rising inflation pressure. RBOB gasoline futures are up about 30% since early August, diesel is nearing $6/gallon, and one-year inflation swaps, a CPI leading indicator, are back to their highest level since mid-June, evidence that consumer prices remain elevated. This is showing up in consumer discretionary: the sector's year-over-year return is negative despite the S&P 500 up about 18% y/y, and apparel, leisure/travel, homebuilders, and equal-weight consumer stocks (RSPD) keep breaking lower. Equal-weight S&P 500 ex-AI fell 1.39%, its worst day in two months, lost its 50-day moving average, and is in its worst drawdown since May, leading BTIG to expect a correlation-one downside event. Private equity/credit stocks, which rallied from early July, have stalled and are rolling over again. Separately, the SOX has bounced about 9% in three days but hasn't reclaimed its 50-day average; BTIG cites SOX's 2000 topping process, crossing its 50-day average ten times over six months before finally breaking down, as a caution against reading the bounce as confirmation. Thesis: bottoms are events, tops are processes.
